column1: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree — given a sorted int array, build a height-balanced BST. Example: [-10,-3,0,5,9] → [0,-3,9,-10,null,5] (one valid balanced answer).
column2: PATTERN: Recursion picking the middle as root. | INSIGHT: Middle element is the root; recurse on left and right halves to build subtrees. | STEPS: build(l,r): 1) If l>r: None. 2) m=(l+r)//2. 3) node=TreeNode(nums[m]). 4) node.left=build(l,m-1); node.right=build(m+1,r). 5) Return node. Call build(0, n-1). | TIME/SPACE: O(n) / O(log n). | PITFALL: Always pick the middle to keep balance — picking start/end loses the height bound.

column1: Sort List — sort a linked list in O(n log n) and ideally O(1) extra space. Example: 4→2→1→3 → 1→2→3→4.
column2: PATTERN: Merge sort on a linked list. | INSIGHT: Split with slow/fast pointers; recursively sort halves; merge. | STEPS: 1) If not head or not head.next: return head. 2) Find mid: slow,fast=head,head.next; while fast and fast.next: slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next.next. 3) mid=slow.next; slow.next=None. 4) left=sort(head); right=sort(mid). 5) Return merge(left,right) (standard merge two sorted lists). | TIME/SPACE: O(n log n) / O(log n) recursion (true O(1) space needs bottom-up iterative merge sort). | PITFALL: Cut the list properly: prev_of_mid.next=None.

column1: Construct Quad Tree — given an n×n binary grid (n is a power of 2), build its quad tree. A node is a leaf if its region is uniform; otherwise split into 4 equal quadrants. Example: 4×4 grid with 4 differing quadrants → root with 4 leaf children.
column2: PATTERN: Recursive 4-way split. | INSIGHT: If region is uniform → leaf with that value; else split into 4 quadrants and recurse. | STEPS: build(r,c,size): 1) If region uniform (all cells same): return Node(val, isLeaf=True). 2) half=size//2. 3) tl=build(r,c,half); tr=build(r,c+half,half); bl=build(r+half,c,half); br=build(r+half,c+half,half). 4) Return Node(*, isLeaf=False, tl, tr, bl, br). | TIME/SPACE: O(n²) / O(n²) worst. | PITFALL: Uniform check itself is region-sized; the recursion structure keeps total work manageable.

column1: Merge k Sorted Lists — given k sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted list. Example: [[1,4,5],[1,3,4],[2,6]] → 1→1→2→3→4→4→5→6.
column2: PATTERN: Min-heap of (val, list_index, node) — or divide-and-conquer pairwise merging. | INSIGHT (heap): Always extract the smallest current head and replace with its next. Heap holds at most k elements. | STEPS (heap): 1) heap = [(node.val, i, node) for i,node in enumerate(lists) if node]; heapify. 2) dummy=ListNode(); cur=dummy. 3) While heap: v,i,node=heappop; cur.next=node; cur=cur.next; if node.next: heappush(heap,(node.next.val, i, node.next)). 4) Return dummy.next. | TIME/SPACE: O(N log k) / O(k). | PITFALL: Include the list index `i` as a tiebreaker — ListNode itself isn't comparable.
